answer.authorDates: 1940–1980 · English musician, co-founder of the Beatles & peace activist
answer.sourceLine: These are the words of the chorus of “Imagine,” written by John Lennon and released in 1971 on the album and single of the same name. The line is genuine and correctly attributed; since 2017 Yoko Ono — whose 1964 book Grapefruit Lennon credited as the source of the “lyric and concept” — shares the official songwriting credit.

source.excerpt: Imagine all the people living life in peace. You may say I’m a dreamer, but I’m not the only one. I hope someday you’ll join us, and the world will live as one.
trail: The song was written and recorded by John Lennon in 1971 and released that autumn, per Wikipedia’s article on “Imagine” ↗.
John Lennon’s official single page ↗ prints the chorus containing this exact line.
Lennon said “several poems from Yoko Ono’s 1964 book Grapefruit inspired” the lyric, and in 2017 Ono received a co-writing credit — both documented on Wikipedia ↗.
source.excerptNote: The chorus of “Imagine.” Reproduced here in brief for identification; the song remains under copyright.
source.rightsHolder: The Estate of John Lennon and Yoko Ono (published through Lenono Music)
source.rightsNote: “Imagine” was first published in 1971 and remains firmly under copyright in the United States. The composition is controlled by John Lennon’s estate and Yoko Ono through Lennon’s publishing company, Lenono Music; the sound recording rights sit with the album’s label. This line may be quoted briefly for commentary, but the lyric is not in the public domain.

author.bio: John Lennon (1940–1980) was an English singer, songwriter and peace activist who rose to worldwide fame as a co-founder of the Beatles. His 1971 solo album Imagine and its title track became an enduring anthem of pacifism and utopian hope. Lennon was shot and killed in New York City in December 1980.

misattribution.heading: The credit question
misattribution.intro: The line is correctly remembered as John Lennon’s — but there is a genuine authorship nuance worth knowing.

items.why: For decades the song was credited to Lennon alone. Lennon later said its “lyric and concept” came “straight out of” Ono’s 1964 book Grapefruit, and in June 2017 the National Music Publishers Association recognised her as a co-author, per Wikipedia ↗.
The line circulates on social media as a free-floating “dreamer” slogan detached from the song, which obscures that it is a copyrighted 1971 lyric, not a public-domain proverb.

misattribution.truthLine: It really is Lennon — the chorus of “Imagine” (1971) — with Yoko Ono now a credited co-writer, per the song’s history ↗.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: “Imagine” asks listeners to picture a world without borders, possessions or religion, and this couplet is its emotional hinge: Lennon concedes he may sound naive, then insists his hope is shared. That turn — from ‘dreamer’ to ‘not the only one’ — is what made the line a rallying cry for peace movements for half a century.
detailsBody: The recording was added to the U.S. National Recording Registry in 2023, one marker of its lasting cultural weight.
